title: Studying Scripture
definition: Studying Scripture is the faithful practice of reading, observing, interpreting, and applying the written Word of God with reverence, humility, prayer, and obedience.
summary: Bible study is not merely gathering information; it is sitting under God's authority and responding to His Word.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the center and fulfillment of Scripture, and faithful study leads the heart to behold Him, trust Him, and follow Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Studying Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to studying scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
